- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.05) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Lagged corrections: if recent sentiment turns negative, model often doesn’t adjust forecast downward until 2–3 days later.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: model overreacts to short-term spikes, then overcorrects downward — create a “peak-pullback” buffer.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes trend continues, but true price often reverts to 30-day moving average within 5–7 days — apply smoothing or decay factor.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June–July) — reduce forecast slope if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model still pushes up — cap forecast increase if sentiment <0.10.
